english.title: Aid abet counsel procure the causing of death by driving a vehicle - driver unlicensed / uninsured
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), aided, abetted, counselled and procured, **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), in causing the death of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF DECEASED AND DATE OF DEATH IF DIFFERENT FROM DATE OF DRIVING..) by driving a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ROAD..), at a time when circumstances were such that

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

was committing an offence under

(C)_[section 87(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 by driving the vehicle otherwise than in accordance with a licence authorising the driving of a motor vehicle of that class]_
(D)_[section 103(1)(b) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 by driving when disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle of that class]_

Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) IMPORTANT NOTE - Causing death by driving a vehicle when disqualified (option [D]) is no longer covered by this offence and this option should only be selected if the offence in question took place prior to 13th April 2015. For any such offence committed after 13th April 2015, offence document H12083 (RT88530) should be used
(ii) SI 2019/1047 Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 remove the current securities regime, which is used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. Therefore, whilst new securities cannot be issued after the 01/11/2019, the SI provides for a transitional period of up to two years (until 1st November 2021) for existing securities and deposits. This means that new securities may not be issued, however that does not prevent individuals renewing current securities - as long as they are valid until 1st November 2021. After this period (or earlier of the security / deposit holder chooses ) compulsory motor insurance will be required.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the words "12 months" shall be omitted (section 61(5) Road Safety Act 2006). Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points.Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneOn the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
